Resolves #18930

The rail-iframe drag arms now press only once the dock is at rest. The control arm (`DockRailRevealIframe.spec.mjs:221`) read the source row's rect while the dock's first layout was still gliding into place. In every failure the row was read at `y=413`, and it had reached `y=53` by the press. The press then hit the empty pane below the row, so no `dragstart` fired and the frame never saw a drop. `dragRowIntoPlainFrame()` now takes both points from `restingPoints()`. It reads the same two signals as `DockTabReorderGesture`'s `restingTab()`: no `neo-dashboard-dock-animating` in the workspace, and no running animations under it.

Evidence: L2 (component tier, real Chromium, repeated runs) → L2 required (a component-tier flake). Residual: none.

Micro-review eligible: test-only. One helper and one call site, with no source change.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | the control arm, `--repeat-each=200`: 200 passed. On `dev` it failed 4 of 80 in a diagnostic copy, and each failure pressed the pane (`mousedown@div#dock-rail-iframe-pane-source`, no `dragstart`) after reading the row mid-glide |
| AC-2 | the whole spec, `--repeat-each=10`: 60 passed. The reveal arm still asserts the drop, the shield lifted by `dragstart`, and the dismissal |
| AC-3 | `restingPoints()` polls the motion signal and `getAnimations({subtree: true})`, with no fixed wait |

## Deltas from ticket

- None.

## Test Evidence

- The diagnostic run behind the ticket recorded, per run, the rect at measure time, the rect at the press, and `elementFromPoint` at the press. The frame document was ready in every run, which rules out the frame as the cause.

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-18T17:16:46Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** micro / test-only — one helper and one call site in a single spec, `+36/−4`, no source change. Per guide §6.4 the light form is the rule here.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** The diagnosis carries this, and it is specific in the way a flake report usually is not: the row was read at `y=413` and had reached `y=53` by the press, so the press landed on the pane below it — with `elementFromPoint` at the press showing `mousedown@div#dock-rail-iframe-pane-source` and no `dragstart`. That is the whole causal chain, measured rather than inferred, and it also rules out the frame (ready in every run), which is the suspect a reader would otherwise reach for first.

**The fix is stronger than the body claims, and the extra strength is the part worth naming.** *"Takes both points from `restingPoints()`"* undersells it: both centres are computed inside **one** `page.evaluate`, so source and target come from a single resting moment. The old code made two separate `boundingBox()` calls, which could straddle the glide even if each individually landed at rest — a second failure mode the rewrite closes silently. Worth knowing it is closed on purpose.

**It reuses the rest signal rather than inventing one.** `restingTab()` in `DockTabReorderGesture.spec.mjs:70` reads the same two signals and is already used twice in that spec (`:110`, `:132`). The helper checks the class on the host, its ancestors **and** its descendants, plus `getAnimations({subtree: true})`, and returns `null` while either says motion — so the poll is on a real signal with no fixed wait, which is also what keeps `check-fixed-sleeps` happy.

**What I looked for and did not find:** a leftover `.width` / `.height` reference. The helper returns `{x, y}` centres, so any surviving `source.width` would quietly become `NaN` and move the pointer nowhere. Only `.x` and `.y` remain at the call site. I also checked that `points` holds the successful iteration's value rather than a stale one — it is assigned inside the poll closure and read after it resolves, so it does.

23/23 green, MERGEABLE, close-target #18930 not `epic`-labeled (`[bug, ai, testing, dashboard]`).

**Findings:** None.
